Subject: Post-demo: deployment mode check for CartLuxe (hosted evaluation follow-up)

Hi Elena / Marco —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can scope the right evaluation path (hosted vs dedicated / private). I attached a short quickstart playbook that outlines the sandbox endpoints and common ops steps.

What we heard on the call:
- Primary goal: power product search personalization + instant chat assist on the storefront.
- Sensitive PII is not stored but order IDs and partial customer names are passed in prompts for personalization.
- Traffic profile estimate (you mentioned): ~120 QPS peak across storefront, average 256 tokens per request during peak.
- Residency: EU-first preference; not strictly required for the initial pilot, but important for production.

Questions to validate deployment mode:
1) Pilot scope — do you want to start with hosted API sandbox (fastest path) or prefer we provision Dedicated capacity from day one because you expect production-like traffic during the trial?
2) Data & residency — will any regulated data be included in pilot prompts, or can you scrub PII until you move to a VPC/Private deployment?
3) SSO / network allowlist — can you share the IP ranges and SAML IdP details (I attached an example spreadsheet)?

Quick notes on hosted trial capabilities (summary):
- Quickstart endpoints: sandbox.redwood.ai/cartluxe/{chat,generation,embeddings} (non-prod)
- Default sandbox rate caps: 60 RPS (burst to 90 for short windows) and token-based throughput limits; we can provision higher slices for pilots by request.
- Persistent features available in hosted: prefix KV caching, streaming responses, and request-level encryption in transit.
- If you need guaranteed throughput or private networking for pilot traffic, Dedicated or Private (VPC) are options — we can provide a cost/latency comparison after you confirm expected qps & steady-state tokens/sec.

Next steps from us:
- If hosted sandbox is OK, we’ll provision a CartLuxe sandbox with test keys and a short runbook (attached).
- If you prefer Dedicated, we’ll prepare a rough capacity estimate and pricing delta for your expected peak and typical sequences.

Can you confirm preferred pilot mode and share the SSO/IP spreadsheet when convenient? I can loop in Aditya for pricing and Vivek for ops/throughput planning.

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment mode check for CartLuxe (hosted evaluation follow-up)

Hi Chloe —

Thanks for the clear summary and the playbook — useful. A few answers and notes from our side:

1) Pilot preference: We’d prefer to start on Hosted to move faster and validate quality/latency with real traffic. If the pilot shows we need steady high throughput + guaranteed SLAs we’ll move to Dedicated, but we don’t want to commit capacity yet.

2) Data: For the initial pilot we can scrub PII and use hashed order IDs. Production will require EU residency for stored artifacts, but we expect to manage that when we move to Dedicated/Private.

3) Traffic clarifications: The 120 QPS was a rough peak for peak shopping hours. Typical steady-state for us is ~25–35 QPS. Average tokens per request during peak might be closer to 220 (earlier 256 was conservative). We’ll validate with engineering and send a tighter number.

4) Ops ask: Can hosted sandbox support the prefix/KV caching you mentioned? Caching is important for pricing.

We’ll attach our SSO / allowlist info in a follow-up once I confirm with infra (likely later today).

Elena
Head of Product
CartLuxe

Hi Elena — great notes. A couple of concrete items from pricing/ops side so you have expectations for the hosted trial: 

- Hosted sandbox baseline: 60 RPS per endpoint (we classify chat/generation separately) with token-throttling. For the profile you described (25–35 steady, 120 peak), hosted trial is a good fit.
- Pilot burst handling: we can grant a temporary burst allowance up to 120 RPS for short periods (we monitor and expire bursts after 24–72 hours unless you request an extension).
- KV/prefix caching: available in hosted sandbox — caching reduces billed tokens on repeated prefixes but doesn't change the throughput caps; it often reduces cost materially for personalization workloads.
- When you’re ready for production: Dedicated pricing usually becomes value-add when sustained peak >80–100 RPS with low-latency SLOs or when you need isolated GPUs for compliance. We’ll draft a quick cost delta for your expected traffic.

Technical sync suggestion: Vivek can run a 30-minute ops/throughput session to validate token shapes and choose endpoint mapping (chat vs generation, separate embeddings pipeline). Monica can run a short success-plan to align success metrics. 

Actionable: Chloe / Elena — if you confirm hosted sandbox, we’ll:
1) Provision sandbox keys + scoped endpoints and share onboarding runbook (24–48h)
2) Grant a temporary burst to 120 RPS for two test windows
3) Schedule a 30-min ops sync with Vivek

I’ll attach a compact rate-plan reference doc (internal stub) here for your review.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
